cases.name: built-in worked example
stdout: (no config - demo: the three options on illustrative numbers over 12 months, and a fit check for a seed-stage team)
COMPARE - over 12 months, your time at 150 an hour. Nothing here is a benchmark.
In-house hire: 247,990 total; starts in 2 mo; 8.5 productive months; 29,175 per productive month; 87 of your hours
salary 150,000, load 45,000, recruiting 36,000, tools 4,000, yourTime 12,990
Fractional leader (cheapest): 176,388 total; starts now; 11.5 productive months; 15,338 per productive month; 104 of your hours
retainer 120,000, execution 36,000, tools 4,800, yourTime 15,588
Agency: 184,976 total; starts now; 11.0 productive months; 16,816 per productive month; 208 of your hours
retainer 144,000, setup 5,000, tools 4,800, yourTime 31,176

Crossover: The in-house hire never becomes the cheaper option: once both are running it costs 6,500 more per month than the fractional leader, so the gap only widens. Check the salary load and the execution line; those are the two people usually get wrong.
If you stop at month 6:
In-house hire: spent 115,600, still owed 0. Recruiting again, and the replacement ramps from zero. No severance assumed.
Fractional leader: spent 80,400, still owed 13,000. 1-month notice, then it stops.
Agency: spent 79,400, still owed 0. Minimum term already served.

FIT - FRACTIONAL-PLUS-EXECUTION: Judgement is part-time (10 hours) but execution is not (25 hours) and nobody in-house does it. A strategy-only retainer will not write the emails: pair a fractional leader with a contractor or a junior hire, and count both.
